title: Tony Leung Talks to Trees Now — and a New Movie Explains Why
summary: What if trees could feel things — just like you and me? That's a question Hong Kong star Tony Leung started asking after making his new movie, "Silent Friend." In the film, he plays a brain scientist named Dr. Tony Wong. During the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic, he gets stuck in Germany studying a ginkgo tree. He's trying to understand if trees can communicate or even have feelings. To prepare for the role, Leung read books about plant intelligence. And guess what? It totally changed his mind. "I see them as sentient beings, same like me, same like human beings," he said. Sentient means able to feel things. The movie is directed by Ildikó Enyedi, who also made the Oscar-nominated "On Body and Soul." It tells three stories connected to the same tree, set in different time periods. Leung's story takes place in 2020, but there's also one in 1908 and another in 1972. Leung is famous for romantic films like "In the Mood for Love," but this is his first European movie. He said he never planned to work outside Asia — he just follows interesting directors. Now, after playing a tree scientist, he looks at every plant with new respect. Next time you see a tree, maybe you'll wonder what it's thinking, too.
why_it_matters: It might make you think differently about the trees and plants around you — maybe they're more alive and aware than you realized.

background_read: Tony Leung is one of Hong Kong's most famous actors, known for romantic movies like 'In the Mood for Love' and many action films.
The ginkgo tree is sometimes called a 'living fossil' because it has hardly changed for millions of years and can survive in cities around the world.
Director Ildikó Enyedi also made 'On Body and Soul', which was nominated for an Oscar, and she enjoys telling unusual and magical stories.
Article_Structure: WHO: Tony Leung, who plays a brain scientist named Dr. Tony Wong
WHAT: A movie called 'Silent Friend' about a ginkgo tree connecting three different time periods and a scientist who sees trees as sentient
WHERE: Set in Germany, with scenes in 1908, 1972, and 2020
WHY: To explore whether trees can feel and communicate, and how that idea changes the scientist's view of nature

perspectives.description: People who care about the environment are happy that a big movie is asking if plants have feelings, because it could lead to more respect for nature.
Many scientists say that while plants do amazing things, we still can't prove they are truly sentient like animals, so the movie's idea is still a big question.
Some viewers see the ginkgo tree not just as a plant but as a symbol linking human stories across time, showing how everything is connected.
